headline: Bank deputy says rate rise ‘increasingly likely’ if energy prices stay high
summary: A Bank of England deputy said a rate rise is increasingly likely if energy prices stay high. UK inflation rose to a five-month high of 3.1 last month, moving further from the Bank's 2 per cent target.
why: The Bank of England sets UK interest rates, which affect borrowing costs, gilt yields, sterling and equity valuations across the economy.

source.name: East London and West Essex Guardian Series

sources.name: East London and West Essex Guardian Series

why_moved: Inflation rose to 3.1 per cent, further above the 2 per cent target, and a Bank deputy said higher energy prices make a rate rise more likely.
